title: Navigating by command line: prompt, PowerShell and shell

videos.script: The server in the cupboard has no desktop. No Start button, no Dock, no icons. When Ana connects to it, she gets a window with one line of text in it and a blinking cursor. Everything she will ever do on that server, she does from there. {{cursor}} It looks less friendly than a desktop and it is, at first. It is also faster once you know it, and it works the same over a slow connection from home. And a command can be written down, sent to somebody else, and repeated exactly. A sequence of clicks cannot. {{why}} Every system has one. Linux and macOS have a shell, bash or zsh. Windows has two, the old Command Prompt and PowerShell. They look alike, and they differ in ways that matter the first time you type a path with a space in it. {{three}} You will read what a prompt tells you, and move around the folders by absolute and relative paths. You will deal with spaces and with capital letters, and do the same things in PowerShell. Then you will find help for a command you do not know, and see the one idea that makes PowerShell different from every other shell. {{steps}} The transcripts come from lesson 3's server, in bash, and in PowerShell 7 running on that same machine. The Windows and macOS prompts are shown, not run. {{honest}}
